findings.claim: The new wake e2e driver marks correct lazy invitation behavior as a failure because both invitation cases require an idle wake for nudge-only recipients.
findings.evidence: At c211906a8801965efc61f3a90bb9d9de34cfaa6c, Recipient.case sets expect_wake=true for every invite action (scripts/wake-e2e.py:766), sends an unflagged cooperative invite for invite/group (:778), and sends a Lazy direct opening message for invite/1:1 (:782). The driver supplies cooperative top-level claims, without --operator (:180-185). src/cli/commands.rs:2260-2265 therefore assigns Lazy confirmation to that group invitation; src/cli/direct_send.rs:253-257 assigns Lazy confirmation to the pair invitation. src/store/attention.rs:703-726 and :1749-1763 deliberately exclude Lazy invitations from wake work and omit the Lazy message frontier under wake_on=nudge. Thus a correctly idle nudge-only recipient yields woke=false, while :823 requires woke==true and records FAIL even if the subsequent hello delivers and accepts everything. AGENTS.md makes this newly added driver a mandatory pre-release gate, so its oracle rejects the selected lazy-default behavior. This is a source-level mismatch in the imported test driver, independent of whether the deferred authenticated release run has been performed.
